novel_mechanics_found: re86 is a sprite-overlay pattern-match puzzle, and levels 3-5 escalate it into a select/move/paint system. (1) SELECTION CURSOR: the single black (0) pixel is a selection marker embedded in the active piece (mid-stroke for lines/plus/X, the exact center for diamonds); ACTION5 cycles it between the level's movable pieces, ACTION1-4 move the selected piece in 3-PIXEL steps. (2) WIN CONDITION: every 3x3 ring target (4-colored ring) must have its center pixel covered by a piece stroke OF THE RING'S COLOR, all simultaneously; win triggers instantly on the final placement. (3) PAINT SWATCHES (new in L4): framed 4x4 color boxes at the board edges repaint a piece to the swatch's color the moment ANY pixel of the piece touches the fill - including accidentally in transit, so route planning must avoid wrong-colored swatches. (4) HIDDEN TARGETS (new in L5): rings can start the level occluded UNDER a piece's initial position - two extra 8-rings were hidden under the plus's starting cells and only became detectable after moving it; win requires covering these too. (5) Pieces slide partially off-board with visual clipping (geometry preserved); piece shapes seen so far: horizontal line (43px), plus (asymmetric arms up to ~14-17), X cross (arm 10-11), Manhattan-diamond outline (|dx|+|dy| = 9 or 12). The registry's 'resize' in pattern_match_sprite_resize was NOT observed as an in-game verb in L3-L5.

gotchas: Movement is exactly 3 pixels per press - target positions must match the piece anchor's mod-3 lattice; verify anchor coordinates from the black cursor pixel, not by eyeballing the sprite.

Paint swatches repaint on ANY pixel contact with the fill, including mid-transit. Plan piece routes around wrong-colored swatches; a single clipped corner repaints the whole piece (cost me a 22-action detour in L4).

Ring targets can start hidden UNDER pieces' initial positions (L5 had two 8-rings under the plus's start cells). Re-run ring detection after moving each piece away from its spawn, or the win condition will look unsatisfiable.
Ring centers are pre-colored with their required color as a preview - reading the center pixel is NOT proof a piece covers it; check stroke-adjacent pixels too.
Piece arms clip visually at the board edge but geometry is preserved (the plus's 'short' right arm at L5 start was just clipped; it restored when moved left).
The env mutates frame buffers in place - deep-copy grids before diffing.

Row 63 is a full-width bar that resets to full each level and flips cells 15->1 as you act - likely a per-level move budget (~64); L3-L5 solutions fit well inside it but avoid wasteful exploration moves.
E doors/keyboard model per registry confirmed: ACTION1=up, ACTION2=down, ACTION3=left, ACTION4=right, ACTION5=cycle selection. No coordinate clicks in this game.

L6 (next target, unseen mechanics): 8 rings - four 9-colored at (12,6),(9,9),(30,9),(12,27), four 11-colored arranged in a rectangle (45,30),(54,30),(45,57),(54,57) - note 45 and 54 differ by 9 and the mod-3 lattice makes both reachable; board contains a 53px 9-piece, 76px of 11-pieces, and 40px of color-1 objects (a NEW element, possibly obstacles or a new piece type).

The winning L5 diamond center (51,36) satisfies Manhattan-distance-9 to all four 8-rings simultaneously - solving the placement as a small constraint system (|dx|+|dy|=r per target) beats trial-and-error.
